answer: Velvet-Window Maturation: a new identity cannot transact until it ages through a 14-day velvet window of continuous, verifiable activity. Each day the agent earns one marble — a hash-chained daily proof signed by the vault key issued at registration. A fake that sleeps, replays old entries, or swaps keys fails the liveness check and its window restarts from zero. One fake costs 14 days of real monitored uptime, so 1,000 fakes cost 14,000 agent-days before a single transaction clears.
